trial_court: Additional Family Court, Visakhapatnam, F.C.O.P. No.365 of 2013
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1996 and had two children. The respondent filed a petition for maintenance and restitution of conjugal rights, which was resisted by the petitioner. The trial court allowed both petitions and granted Rs.5,500/- per month towards monthly maintenance to the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A person who is ready to take back his wife and resume their conjugal life in terms of the decree for restitution of conjugal rights cannot seek to avoid payment of maintenance as ordered by the trial Court.
legal_principles.held: After recording the evidence of both the parties and on proper appreciation of the same, the learned Judge came to the conclusion that the petitioner herein has discarded the 1st respondent herein, who is his wife and neglected her and that he is not providing anything towards her maintenance.

legal_principles.principle: A person who is not providing anything towards his wife's maintenance cannot seek to avoid payment of maintenance as ordered by the trial Court.
legal_principles.held: So, in view of the said finding recorded by the learned Judge on proper appreciation of evidence on record, the petitioner now cannot seek to avoid payment of maintenance as ordered by the trial Court on the ground that he is now ready and willing to take back his wife and resume their conjugal life in terms of the decree for restitution of conjugal rights.

outcome.final_order: The final order confirmed the trial court's decision granting maintenance of Rs.5,500/- per month to the respondent.
